label: Spinner
title: Spinner
summary: Use a Spinner to show that something is loading when you can't show its shape or say how long it will take.
corePrinciple: Show that something is happening, then get out of the way.

anatomy.title: Three arcs chasing each other
anatomy.description: Three 100° arcs with round ends turn clockwise around an empty centre, with no track behind them. Each is about 18% of the size thick: 12.8 px at the default 72 px, as in Figma. The diagram shows the resting pose so the pins stay put.
blocks: Gold and drawn on top. It leads the turn: fastest over the top, slowest at the bottom.
Purple. It follows the gold arc; the gap between them opens and closes as it turns.
Teal and last in the chain, closing up behind the others at the top of each turn.

configuration.title: Size, speed, and gravity
configuration.description: Three settings shape it: size sets the diameter, durationMs the time for one turn, and gravity how much it speeds up over the top and slows at the bottom. No mode changes it. A colors setting can replace its three colours in code; keep Coin's gold, purple, and teal.
blocks: Gravity 0.45 and a 1.5 s turn: a little faster over the top.
Gravity 0.85 and a 2.8 s turn: fast over the top, slow at the bottom.
Gravity 0 and a 1.6 s turn: the same speed all the way round.

states.title: Spinning or resting
states.description: It spins while animating is on, the default. With animating off, or when the device asks for reduced motion, it rests as an evenly spaced fan of three arcs; the rest isn't a frame of the spin. It has no pressed, focus, or disabled state.
blocks: Shown while something loads; the screen removes it when the content arrives.
Also what people who turn on reduced motion see.

sizing.title: You set the diameter
sizing.description: Size is the diameter in px: 72 by default, with no minimum or maximum. The arcs stay about 18% of it thick, so a 32 px spinner draws 5.7 px arcs. It keeps its size and doesn't stretch to fill its host.
blocks: 5.7 px arcs. Small enough to sit beside a line of text.
10 px arcs, for a card or one section that's loading.
15.6 px arcs, for a whole screen waiting on one thing.

content.title: No text of its own
content.description: The spinner shows no words. Its spoken name is “Loading” unless you set accessibilityLabel; name what's loading, and add a short line of text next to it when the wait is more than a moment.
blocks: A 56 px spinner named “Loading your statements” and one line that says the same.

examples.title: Say what's loading
examples.description: A 56 px spinner named “Loading your statements” and one line that says the same.

inContext.title: Refreshing statements
inContext.description: Refresh swaps the list for a spinner and a line of text while the statements load, then brings the list back. The screen owns the loading state; the spinner only shows it.

doDont.title: One clear wait
doDont.description: Each pair shows a wait people understand next to one that leaves them guessing or watching several spinners at once.
blocks: A short line next to it tells people what they're waiting for.
A spinner on its own says something is happening, not what.
One spinner covers the whole list while it loads.
Several spinners compete for attention and make the wait feel longer.

sources.title: Use the public Spinner contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Spinner is one 72 × 72 frame of three arcs in gold, purple, and teal, with no variants; the motion, speed, gravity, and resting pose exist only in code. Since the #276 fix the arcs match Figma’s ring: 12.8 px thick at 72, and in proportion at other sizes. No mode changes it, and a colors setting replaces its three colours. It is announced as a progress bar named “Loading” unless you name it, with no value. The published Storybook page is still the old generated one.
